findings.summary: All fields are required, but users receive no visible indication of that before submitting.
findings.fix: Add visible text such as “All fields are required” before each form, or mark each required label visibly; keep the native required attributes.
findings.evidence: Every visible input has required, but neither form shows a required-fields instruction or marker.

findings.summary: The setup error is associated with every field, so screen reader users may hear unrelated feedback without knowing which field needs correction.
findings.fix: Identify the field or fields that failed validation, set aria-invalid="true" on those controls, and associate each with its specific visible error using aria-describedby; keep general system errors separate from field errors.
findings.evidence: Each of the six inputs conditionally references the same setup-error paragraph.

findings.summary: The 12-character password instruction is not programmatically associated with either password field.
findings.fix: Give visible password guidance an id and reference it from both password fields using aria-describedby, alongside any field-specific error description.
findings.evidence: The intro states the 12-character minimum, but the password inputs do not reference it.

findings.summary: After a setup validation error, previously entered names, email, and username are cleared and must be entered again.
findings.fix: Republish escaped submitted values for non-password fields after validation errors; continue clearing password fields.
findings.evidence: The setup inputs have no value attributes, despite server-side validation returning the form.

findings.summary: Password fields have no show/hide control, so users cannot verify what they typed before submitting.
findings.fix: Offer an accessible button to show or hide each password, with a clear state announcement; do not interfere with paste or password managers.
findings.evidence: The scoped forms contain password inputs but no visibility toggle.

passed: Visible labels are programmatically associated with each visible input.
Login and setup inputs use native required constraints.
Username/email and password fields use appropriate autocomplete tokens.
Password inputs remain paste-compatible; no paste-blocking behavior was found.
